deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument can affect the availability and integrity of the resource because it controls whether Terraform is allowed to destroy it. A generic security policy can require PREVENT to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorised deletion.

description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: This argument only provides human-readable metadata and does not change access control, encryption, network exposure, authentication, or another security control.

failover_origin.description:
The Origin resource to try when the current origin cannot be reached.
After maxAttempts is reached, the configured failoverOrigin will be used to fulfil the request.

The value of timeout.maxAttemptsTimeout dictates the timeout across all origins.
A reference to a Topic resource.
failover_origin.rationale: This argument primarily controls availability and failover behaviour. The correct failover origin is environment-specific, so there is no generic security-safe value that can be enforced across different deployments.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the EdgeCache resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are primarily used for organisation and resource metadata. Appropriate label keys and values depend on organisational conventions and do not provide a generic security control for this resource.

max_attempts.description:
The maximum number of attempts to cache fill from this origin. Another attempt is made when a cache fill fails with one of the retryConditions.

Once maxAttempts to this origin have failed the failoverOrigin will be used, if one is specified. That failoverOrigin may specify its own maxAttempts,
retryConditions and failoverOrigin to control its own cache fill failures.

The total number of allowed attempts to cache fill across this and failover origins is limited to four.
The total time allowed for cache fill attempts across this and failover origins can be controlled with maxAttemptsTimeout.

The last valid, non-retried response from all origins will be returned to the client.
If no origin returns a valid response, an HTTP 502 will be returned to the client.

Defaults to 1. Must be a value greater than 0 and less than 4.
max_attempts.rationale: This argument controls retry and failover behaviour during cache fills. It mainly affects reliability and latency, and there is no single value that generically improves security across deployments.

name.description:
Name of the resource; provided by the client when the resource is created.
The name must be 1-64 characters long, and match the regular expression [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]* which means the first character must be a letter,
and all following characters must be a dash, underscore, letter or digit.
name.rationale: The resource name is an identifier. Its secure value is deployment-specific, and the provider already enforces the required naming format.

origin_address.description:
A fully qualified domain name (FQDN) or IP address reachable over the public Internet, or the address of a Google Cloud Storage bucket.

This address will be used as the origin for cache requests - e.g. FQDN: media-backend.example.com, IPv4: 35.218.1.1, IPv6: 2607:f8b0:4012:809::200e, Cloud Storage: gs://bucketname

When providing an FQDN (hostname), it must be publicly resolvable (e.g. via Google public DNS) and IP addresses must be publicly routable.  It must not contain a protocol (e.g., https://) and it must not contain any slashes.
If a Cloud Storage bucket is provided, it must be in the canonical "gs://bucketname" format. Other forms, such as "storage.googleapis.com", will be rejected.
origin_address.rationale: The origin address identifies the backend used by the service. Trusted origins are deployment-specific, so enforcing a secure address would require organisation-specific domain, IP, or bucket values rather than a generic platform policy.

port.description:
The port to connect to the origin on.
Defaults to port 443 for HTTP2 and HTTPS protocols, and port 80 for HTTP.
port.rationale: The port is an origin connectivity setting. Secure transport is determined by the protocol, and legitimate encrypted services can use ports other than 443, so a single generic port restriction would not reliably improve security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project identifies where the resource belongs. The appropriate project is organisation-specific, so a generic policy cannot determine a universally secure project value.

protocol.description:
The protocol to use to connect to the configured origin. Defaults to HTTP2, and it is strongly recommended that users use HTTP2 for both security & performance.

When using HTTP2 or HTTPS as the protocol, a valid, publicly-signed, unexpired TLS (SSL) certificate must be presented by the origin server. Possible values: ["HTTP2", "HTTPS", "HTTP"]
protocol.rationale: This argument directly controls whether traffic between Media CDN and the origin is encrypted. HTTP is unencrypted, while HTTP2 and HTTPS require TLS. A generic security policy can disallow HTTP and require encrypted origin communication.

retry_conditions.description:
Specifies one or more retry conditions for the configured origin.

If the failure mode during a connection attempt to the origin matches the configured retryCondition(s),
the origin request will be retried up to maxAttempts times. The failoverOrigin, if configured, will then be used to satisfy the request.

The default retryCondition is "CONNECT_FAILURE".

retryConditions apply to this origin, and not subsequent failoverOrigin(s),
which may specify their own retryConditions and maxAttempts.

Valid values are:

- CONNECT_FAILURE: Retry on failures connecting to origins, for example due to connection timeouts.
- HTTP_5XX: Retry if the origin responds with any 5xx response code, or if the origin does not respond at all, example: disconnects, reset, read timeout, connection failure, and refused streams.
- GATEWAY_ERROR: Similar to 5xx, but only applies to response codes 502, 503 or 504.
- RETRIABLE_4XX: Retry for retriable 4xx response codes, which include HTTP 409 (Conflict) and HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests)
- NOT_FOUND: Retry if the origin returns a HTTP 404 (Not Found). This can be useful when generating video content, and the segment is not available yet.
- FORBIDDEN: Retry if the origin returns a HTTP 403 (Forbidden). Possible values: ["CONNECT_FAILURE", "HTTP_5XX", "GATEWAY_ERROR", "RETRIABLE_4XX", "NOT_FOUND", "FORBIDDEN"]
retry_conditions.rationale: Retry conditions control how the service responds to origin errors. Appropriate conditions depend on application behaviour and availability requirements, and there is no universally secure set that can be enforced generically.

aws_v4_authentication.description: Enable AWS Signature Version 4 origin authentication.

aws_v4_authentication.access_key_id.description: The access key ID your origin uses to identify the key.
aws_v4_authentication.access_key_id.rationale: This value identifies an AWS access key but is not itself the secret credential. The correct identifier is deployment-specific, so a generic policy cannot define a secure value.

aws_v4_authentication.origin_region.description: The name of the AWS region that your origin is in.
aws_v4_authentication.origin_region.rationale: The AWS region must match the actual location of the origin. This is deployment-specific routing and authentication context rather than a value that can be constrained generically for security.

aws_v4_authentication.secret_access_key_.description:
The Secret Manager secret version of the secret access key used by your origin.

This is the resource name of the secret version in the format 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*' where the '*' values are replaced by the project, secret, and version you require.
aws_v4_authentication.secret_access_key_.rationale: This argument references the Secret Manager version containing the AWS secret access key. The provider already requires a Secret Manager secret-version resource name, while the correct project, secret, and version are deployment-specific.

flex_shielding.description:
The FlexShieldingOptions to be used for all routes to this origin.

If not set, defaults to a global caching layer in front of the origin.

flex_shielding.flex_shielding_regions.description:
Whenever possible, content will be fetched from origin and cached in or
near the specified origin. Best effort.

You must specify exactly one FlexShieldingRegion. Possible values: ["AFRICA_SOUTH1", "ME_CENTRAL1"]
flex_shielding.flex_shielding_regions.rationale: This argument controls where origin content is preferentially fetched and cached. It is primarily a performance and location choice, and the appropriate region depends on the deployment rather than a generic security requirement.

origin_override_action.description:
The override actions, including url rewrites and header
additions, for requests that use this origin.

origin_override_action.header_action.description:
The header actions, including adding and removing
headers, for request handled by this origin.

origin_override_action.header_action.req.description:
Describes a header to add.

You may add a maximum of 25 request headers.
The name of the header to add.
origin_override_action.header_action.req.rationale: Header names can have security implications, but the appropriate headers depend on the application and origin. A generic policy cannot define a universally safe required header name without environment-specific context.

origin_override_action.header_action.req.description: The value of the header to add.
origin_override_action.header_action.req.rationale: The correct header value depends on the selected header and the application or origin configuration. Enforcing a particular value would require deployment-specific information rather than a generic platform-level security rule.

origin_override_action.header_action.req.description:
Whether to replace all existing headers with the same name.

By default, added header values are appended
to the response or request headers with the
same field names. The added values are
separated by commas.

To overwrite existing values, set 'replace' to 'true'.
origin_override_action.header_action.req.rationale: Whether an existing header should be replaced or appended depends on the purpose of that header and the origin configuration. Neither boolean value is generically more secure in every deployment.

origin_override_action.url_rewrite.description:
The URL rewrite configuration for request that are
handled by this origin.

origin_override_action.url_rewrite.host_.description:
Prior to forwarding the request to the selected
origin, the request's host header is replaced with
contents of the hostRewrite.

This value must be between 1 and 255 characters.
origin_override_action.url_rewrite.host_.rationale: The host rewrite value must correspond to the intended origin and can also affect the host header and TLS SNI. The correct hostname is deployment-specific, so a generic policy cannot define a universally secure value.

origin_redirect.redirect_conditions.description:
The set of redirect response codes that the CDN
follows. Values of
[RedirectConditions](https://cloud.google.com/media-cdn/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.edgeCacheOrigins#redirectconditions)
are accepted.
origin_redirect.redirect_conditions.rationale: This argument controls when Media CDN follows redirects returned by an origin, including redirects across domains. Following redirects from untrusted or attacker-controlled origins can create open-redirect risk, so a generic security policy can restrict or prohibit redirect following.

timeout.description: The connection and HTTP timeout configuration for this origin.

timeout.connect_timeout.description:
The maximum duration to wait for a single origin connection to be established, including DNS lookup, TLS handshake and TCP/QUIC connection establishment.

Defaults to 5 seconds. The timeout must be a value between 1s and 15s.

The connectTimeout capped by the deadline set by the request's maxAttemptsTimeout.  The last connection attempt may have a smaller connectTimeout in order to adhere to the overall maxAttemptsTimeout.
timeout.connect_timeout.rationale: This timeout controls how long the service waits to establish an origin connection. It mainly affects resilience and performance, and the appropriate value depends on network and application characteristics.

timeout.max_attempts_timeout.description:
The maximum time across all connection attempts to the origin, including failover origins, before returning an error to the client. A HTTP 504 will be returned if the timeout is reached before a response is returned.

Defaults to 15 seconds. The timeout must be a value between 1s and 30s.

If a failoverOrigin is specified, the maxAttemptsTimeout of the first configured origin sets the deadline for all connection attempts across all failoverOrigins.
timeout.max_attempts_timeout.rationale: This timeout controls the total time allowed for origin attempts and failover. It is primarily an availability and latency setting, and there is no single value that generically improves security.

timeout.read_timeout.description:
The maximum duration to wait between reads of a single HTTP connection/stream.

Defaults to 15 seconds.  The timeout must be a value between 1s and 30s.

The readTimeout is capped by the responseTimeout.  All reads of the HTTP connection/stream must be completed by the deadline set by the responseTimeout.

If the response headers have already been written to the connection, the response will be truncated and logged.
timeout.read_timeout.rationale: This timeout controls how long the service waits between reads from the origin. It primarily affects reliability and response handling rather than providing a generic security control.

timeout.response_timeout.description:
The maximum duration to wait for the last byte of a response to arrive when reading from the HTTP connection/stream.

Defaults to 30 seconds. The timeout must be a value between 1s and 120s.

The responseTimeout starts after the connection has been established.

This also applies to HTTP Chunked Transfer Encoding responses, and/or when an open-ended Range request is made to the origin. Origins that take longer to write additional bytes to the response than the configured responseTimeout will result in an error being returned to the client.

If the response headers have already been written to the connection, the response will be truncated and logged.
timeout.response_timeout.rationale: This timeout controls the maximum duration for receiving an origin response. It mainly affects availability and performance, and an appropriate value depends on workload behaviour.
